title: What Happens If You Sit All Day?
description:
Send this to the friend who hasn't left their chair since breakfast.
Mayo Clinic sums up an analysis of 13 studies and more than a million people: sitting more than eight hours a day with no physical activity carried a risk of dying similar to obesity and smoking, and 60 to 75 minutes of moderate activity a day countered it. The UK Department of Health and Social Care calls inactivity a 'silent killer'. Worried about your own health? Talk to a doctor.
Next Body File: what happens to your fingers in the bath.

structure_note: A 'dose' explainer built around one question, how much moving cancels a day in the chair. Frame 1: the hero sinking into an office chair while a wall clock whips from 9 to 5 (7+ HOURS tag) and the A 20 MIN / B HOUR+ pills pop. Then an x-ray-cyan leg with muscle fibres going dark as he sits; the movie-seat cutaway (hero peeling off a cinema seat, rust flakes) for the relatable beat; the re-hook pulls back from the legs to a whole-body x-ray where a 'metabolism' furnace dims; a stopwatch/scale comparison for 8+ hours vs a cigarette icon (schematic only, no smoke clouds or illness imagery); the answer: an hour-glass fills to 60-75 MIN and pill B gets its check; a tiny wall-timer pinging every 30 minutes as he stands; the bath-fingers tease; and the hero sitting back down in the frame-1 chair. Different from the doorway (lab-experiment yes/no), funny-bone (anatomy tour, body-side guess), stand-up (direction guess, name twist) and sneeze (myth-fact cold open) videos: no lab, no body-map guess, no myth stamp; a time/dose guess.
safety: Calm, curious-friend tone. Every body claim is attributed to NHS, Mayo Clinic or NIH; the death-risk line is the Mayo summary of a 13-study analysis (risk similar to obesity and smoking), framed as 'eight-plus hours, no exercise'. The one tip is Mayo's ('stand every 30 minutes'), voiced as Mayo's, not as personal advice; the description adds 'talk to a doctor'. No weight targets, no calorie counts, no diet advice (BIBLE). Smoking appears only as a comparison icon, never as a how-to or a realistic illness image.
